subject: a question about ts_par7: the absolute value of "w" and "Lambda" change with different sample size

messages.author: c6324df9150c60dc
messages.subject: a question about ts_par7: the absolute value of "w" and "Lambda" change with different sample size
parts:
Hi hbayesdm team, 
    Thank you develop such a useful and convenient tool.   
   I am new on model fitting, I was trying to fit a Hybrid Model using ts_par7 in hBayesDM with data from our two-stage decision task (using the Daw paradigm,alomost the same really). However I found that the fitted "w" (model-based weight) and the "lambda" (eligibility trace) can change drmaticlly according to the sample I used. .I tried five different samples: each has different sample size but every has the same 10 subjects as in "PETSI_HC72210subsample2019.txt ". And I fitted the ts_par7 of these sample using following code: 
Results<-ts_par7(data = "PETSI_HC72210subsample2019.txt ", niter = 4000, nwarmup = 1000, nchain = 4,
        ncore = 1, nthin = 1, inits = "fixed", indPars = "mean",
        modelRegressor = FALSE, vb = FALSE,
        inc_postpred = FALSE, adapt_delta = 0.95, stepsize = 1,
        max_treedepth = 10, trans_prob = 0.7) 
The fitted parameters of the 10 subjects were roughly identcal in the five fittings, except the "w" and "lambda".These two parameters seems much more dispersed than the other five. The fitted parameters can be found in the excel file.  However, the "w" and "lambda" are the most important parameters in this project. I really want to know how much the subjects are "model-based" in their decision.
My questions are: 
Is there anything I did wrong in using ts_par7,maybe the arguments I used? 
if there is some kind of sample size limitation in fitting such a model? for instance,how many sample do I need to get a reliable results?
if there were some outliers in my sample? How can I identify these outliers?
Any help will be appreciated. 
Best regards！
                                        Wei Lei
